messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-98421 — EDGE: TLS handshake failure rate spike detected (>10% in eu-west-1). URL: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-98421
Maria Chen: seeing 502/524s in EU service logs; spikes started ~02:29 UTC. Not user-wide but affecting several large customers behind eu-west ALBs.
Jonah Patel: confirmed — cloudwatch: tls_handshake_errors up from 0.3% -> 12% for edge-proxy-eu-*. Backend targets show Unhealthy counts rising (5/6 unhealthy in some AZs).
pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-98421 created and auto-notified on-call. Escalation timer set (5m).
Sam Rivera: ack. I'm oncall and taking this. Jumping into proxies and certs. Sam Rivera here.
Tara O'Neill: fyi we rotated edge certs at 02:30 UTC for staging->prod promotion; DNS CNAMEs were updated with TTL=60. Could be propagation / wrong cert served.
Sam Neteng: we pushed cert rotation + updated cert alias on edge-na/eu listeners. Some edge nodes still returning old cert chain for SNI api.redwood.com in eu-west-1 — investigating why cache didn't invalidate.
Maria Chen: stack traces show TLS alert 40/handshake_failure, SNI mismatch: client sees certificate CN=staging.internal.redwood.
Jonah Patel: pulled a packet capture from one healthy and one unhealthy node. unhealthy node serving older cert with issuer chain that doesn't include new root.
Sam Rivera: running quick check: `openssl s_client -connect edge-eu1:443 -servername api.redwood.com -showcerts` — confirms old cert on edge-eu1-azb.
Sam Neteng: looks like config apply failed on a subset of instances during the orchestration bump. Some listeners rolled back while others completed.
Lisa Gomez: CS: we have two customers reporting 500s and one Revenue API partner with partial outage. Estimating ~8-15% of EU traffic affected, mostly long connections hitting TLS handshake.
Maria Chen: mitigation plan: 1) remove weight from unhealthy LB targets in eu-west-1, 2) force certificate reload on edge nodes that didn't pick up new cert, 3) rollback to previous cert if reload fails. Will coordinate.
Jonah Patel: adding commands: to remove weight -> `aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false` (example), and patch listeners to point back to previous cert-arn.
Sam Neteng: I'm SSHing to the failing nodes to trigger `nginx -s reload` and validate cert symlink. If reload fails, we'll replace with previous cert symlink and restart.
incident-bot: Added responders: Sam Rivera, Sam Neteng, Jonah Patel, Maria Chen.
Sam Rivera: executing step 1: setting target weight=0 for failing targets in eu-west-1. Will monitor 1m after each change.
Maria Chen: after first weight drop, 502s dropped by ~60% for that cluster. Still residual errors from other AZ.
Tara O'Neill: neteng — any DNS records pointing to old edge IPs lingering? We changed CNAMEs but some intermediate caches may still map to old nodes.
Sam Neteng: TTL was 60 but some CDNs cached; also internal proxy cache held older certs for 10m. I'm forcing reloads and invalidating local caches.
Jonah Patel: pushing a temporary traffic shift: add weight to healthy regional pool in eu-central and reduce eu-west until nodes stabilized. Updating routing policy now.
Lisa Gomez: customer comms: notifying impacted customers with ETA ~30m, asking to retry requests. Calling our top partner to inform them directly.
Sam Rivera: forced cert reload succeeded on 3/4 affected nodes. One node returned error on reload — rolling that node out of service and reprovisioning.
Maria Chen: health checks back to normal on the clusters we restarted. TLS error rate down to 0.6% in eu-west.
Jonah Patel: confirming by curl test: `curl -v https://api.redwood.com --resolve api.redwood.com:443:3.8.4.2` now returns correct cert chain showing CN=api.redwood.com (prod).
incident-bot: pagerduty PD-98421 auto-escalation cancelled — incident acknowledged and mitigation in progress.
Lisa Gomez: CS update: we've sent targeted messages to affected customers; no major revenue-impacting customers on full outage; one partner saw degraded throughput.
Tara O'Neill: root cause hypothesis: partial rollout of cert alias during orchestration with race where some edge machines reverted to previous symlink path; combined with CDN/internal caches produced intermittent SNI mismatch until reloads/rollbacks applied.
Sam Neteng: follow-ups: add a post-deploy validation job to query 10% of edge nodes across AZs for cert CN, implement a force-reload hook on failed apply, and increase observability for certificate apply success/fail metrics.
Sam Rivera: infra action items: 1) reprovision failed node and run full config apply; 2) publish incident timeline; 3) schedule postmortem with neteng and deploy infra. Handoff to daytime oncall in 45m.
Maria Chen: capturing logs & saving packet captures to central incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/PD-98421/.
Jonah Patel: adding brief: Impact: ~10% EU traffic experienced TLS handshake errors for ~22 minutes. Mitigation: target weight removal + cert reloads + traffic shift. Next steps: postmortem + deployment safeguards.
Lisa Gomez: marking customers updated. Closing comms loop after postmortem.
Sam Rivera: handing off to @daytime-oncall. I’ll be available if any regressions bubble up. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Thread closed for on-call handoff; incident remains active in PagerDuty for postmortem tracking.
